notes: Shared producer-reference corpus for the failure taxonomy: ONE fixture set read by BOTH consumers of FailureClass::classify (src/verdict.rs). The classify tests pin the classifier to `expected_class`; the producer-parity test executes the reference producer's own classification snippet (contrib/argo/gantry-verify-workflowtemplate.yml) on every entry and must stamp the same class. `messages` is the archived cargo JSON protocol stream (one object per line, mixed with the harness's human lines that share stdout); `run_log` is the human-visible run output. `expected_class` is the kebab-case class both implementations must stamp, null where the classifiable window leaves the class unset. `producer_attribute` is set only where the producer attributes the class explicitly (gates) instead of deriving it: classify never derives gate-failure.

entries.name: compile-error-from-the-protocol-stream
entries.why: rustc never finished: an error-level compiler-message in the protocol stream is a compile error whatever else the stream shows (a warning and a build-script record ride along, the way a real failing build does), and the run log carries the rendered diagnostics with no test result at all.

entries.name: compile-error-outranks-later-stream-evidence
entries.why: detection order is the producer's exactly: compile-error outranks everything a later stage printed, because rustc never finished and whatever failed after it is noise (here: overflow AND a failed doc section in the run log).

Doc-tests gantry
test result: FAILED. 0 passed; 1 failed

entries.name: stack-overflow-harness-panic-from-the-run-log
entries.why: a test binary crashed the harness (stack overflow), which the protocol stream never names — the class is read off the human run log and outranks the FAILED lines a partially-completed target printed before dying. The exit code is cargo's (101: some test binary failed), not the crashed binary's signal code.

entries.name: doctest-when-only-the-doc-section-failed
entries.why: the lib target passed and the only FAILED `test result:` lines are the ones after the `Doc-tests` section header. A failing doctest assertion never produces an error-level compiler-message, so the protocol stream is benign here, as in a real instrumented run.

entries.name: mixed-unit-and-doc-failures-are-a-plain-test-failure
entries.why: a run whose unit tests failed AND whose doctests failed is a plain test failure: the doctest class names runs where the doc section was the ONLY thing that failed, so 'also fix your doctests' never hides the real signal.

entries.why: a failed unit test with no compile error, no panic, no Doc-tests section: everything else is a plain test failure.

entries.name: garbled-protocol-lines-cannot-blind-the-classifier
entries.why: leniency the classifier is documented for: a line in the archived protocol stream that is not a JSON object is skipped, not an error — one garbled line cannot blind the classifier to the error-level diagnostic that follows.

entries.name: passing-suite-has-no-failure-to-name
entries.why: a passing suite (exit 0) has no failure to name, even with error-level compiler-messages archived: the window gate dominates whatever the streams show.

entries.name: command-not-found-window-parity
entries.why: exit 127 is command-not-found: the producer later intercepts it as infra and never reads the class it derives here, but the window predicate itself is `exit != 0 && exit < 128` on BOTH sides — this fixture pins the predicate, so 'fixing' either side alone shows up as drift.

entries.name: exit-128-boundary-is-classless
entries.why: 128 is the window's first signal exit: the gate is `exit != 0 && exit < 128` on BOTH sides, so a boundary drift to `<= 128` admits this run and stamps a class classify refuses — the one exit where the two sides must disagree about the gate, not just the class.

entries.name: signal-killed-suite-is-infra
entries.why: a signal-killed suite (exit >= 128; 137 is SIGKILL, conventionally the OOM killer) is infra, classified by the verdict ladder — not a failure class.

entries.name: oom-killed-suite-is-infra-never-a-failure-class
entries.why: the OOM scenario: the run log is a suite cut mid-run by the OOM killer (no test result line, no compiler error, nothing to name), and 137 is the SIGKILL the OOM killer leaves behind. The window gate must leave the class unset because without it this fixture falls through to test-failure — exactly the tests-failed misread an out-of-memory run must never get; the verdict ladder owns it (the producer flags 137 oom on top and stamps the exit-2 infra document).

entries.name: signal-exit-has-no-class-even-on-overflow-evidence
entries.why: even a stack-overflowed log stays unclassified in the signal range: the producer derives classes only under its `exit < 128` gate, so a class read at >=128 would name a run the producer records as class-less — the ladder's InfraFailure is the whole story.

entries.name: uninstrumented-run-has-no-taxonomy
entries.why: a caller-chosen --message-format (instrumented false) means the raw protocol was never captured and no class is derivable — instrumentation must not fight the argv; the exit-code ladder decides, honestly.

entries.name: gate-failure-is-attributed-not-derived
entries.why: gates run only after a PASSING suite, so the taxonomy window derives nothing here on either side; the producer attributes gate-failure explicitly (emit_verdict Failed 0 gate-failure false — the suite's exit 0 stays the truth) and classify never derives it from the streams.
